Vs.

full_judgment: "From the decisions quoted above it is clear that when a party had got a right of appeal against the order he should go for an appeal, he cannot maintain an application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for reversal of the ex parte order. In the instant case, the learned Munsif did exercise his jurisdiction with material irregularity in allowing the said application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure. It was just and proper for restoration of a case under Order 9 r. 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure but it is not just and proper to entertain the application for restoration under Order 9, rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure and under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Order 9, rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure provides for the plaintiff to bring a fresh suit which is dismissed either for non-service of summons in consequence of plaintiffs failure to pay cost or for non-appearance of both the plaintiff and defendants. In this connection, an application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure is also not maintainable, because inherent power of the court exists only where there is no express provision of law applicable to the case. The provisions of this section cannot be invoked to defeat the provisions of the Code nor can be invoked to further injustice or to condone gross negligence. The court cannot interfere under section 151 of the Code with appealable order."
